texts: lotus, sword, humble serving
The lotus bows its head to the water and the sword lays itself down at the guru's feet; the humble hands that serve are the greatest.

Write a doha saying that a proud warrior who sets aside his sword and quietly serves the guru becomes like a lotus that blooms in still water, because the greatest strength is in the humility of the one who serves.
My grandfather was a soldier with a fierce reputation, but in his old age he spent every morning sweeping the guru's courtyard in silence, and I want a doha about the lotus-like peace of that.
doha pls: a warrior laid down his sword to serve the guru and bloomed like a lotus
Blessed are the hands that wash the saints' feet without a thought of reward; they wash away the dust of their own pride.
My mother spends every morning cooking for the poor outside the gurdwara without ever mentioning it to anyone, and I want to write her a doha.
Compose a doha that says the one who serves a saint with a pure heart, without wanting honour or merit in return, receives a gift greater than any treasure, and loses the weight of his own ego.
serve the saints
doha idea: serve the saints without expecting anything
doha pls: serving the poor is the highest prayer, nothing else compares
The hands that feed the hungry are holier than the lips that recite; the heart that serves has found the Lord.
Please craft a couplet that says to feed the hungry and to clothe the naked, with no hope of thanks or reward, is a worship more true than any chanting, because it comes without pride.
I volunteered at a shelter last winter, ladling soup for strangers I'd never see again, and went back to my room feeling lighter than I had in years; make a doha of it.
help the needy

I want a doha that says the person who serves his guru with total humility, without thinking about himself, finds that the guru's wisdom flows into him like water filling an empty vessel without being asked.
hey doha idea: serve your guru like you've got nothing to prove, and everything comes
My teacher never taught me with words, but I swept his room and carried his books for a year, and by the end I understood everything; write a doha.
serve the guru
Bow low before the guru, and let your pride dissolve; the empty heart is filled.
The shrine bell rings out but the one who serves in silence is heard by the Lord; louder than any bell is the hush of humble work.
The old man who rings the bell at our shrine each dawn has done so for fifty years without once asking for a thank-you; write a doha about his kind of service.

Please compose a doha that says the sound of a bell calls the faithful to the shrine, but the Lord is truly pleased by the silent one who sweeps, fetches and serves without any desire for recognition.
doha pls: ringing a bell is easy, but quietly serving others is what God hears
bell, silent serving
doha pls: the musk deer carries a scent it doesn't know about, like a true server who doesn't know how good they are
The musk deer knows not its own fragrance, and the true server knows not his own virtue.

Write a doha that says the humble server is like the musk deer who carries a sweet scent without knowing it, giving help to everyone yet never counting it, and the Lord notices it though no one else does.
The nurse who cared for my mother in her last weeks had a quiet kindness she herself didn't notice, like a musk deer carrying its scent; write a doha.
musk deer, selfless giving
The bridge bears every footstep and asks no thanks, and the elephant lifts the weak upon his back; so the servant carries all.

Make me a doha that says a servant of the needy is like a bridge that lets everyone cross to the other bank without asking their name, and like the elephant who bears the heaviest loads without complaint.
bridge, elephant, serving
The village mason built a bridge across the stream for free, and the village elephant carried the materials, and when it was done no one even thanked them; write a doha.
doha pls: be a bridge for others, carry them like an elephant, and don't ask for thanks
After my father's stroke, I spent a year feeding him, bathing him and keeping him company, and I came to see it as the best thing I ever did; write a doha.
I want a doha showing that when a person serves the old, the sick and the helpless with his own hands, he is doing the work of the Lord, and the humility he learns is worth more than any learning.
Serving the weak with tender hands, I found the Lord was the one being served.
doha about seva being the best way to pray, short pls
care for the helpless
doha pls: a mirror shows your pride, a winnowing fan blows it away, serve others and your ego goes
The mirror shows the face of pride; the winnowing fan blows away the husk; in service the ego is sifted out.
I used to look at my mirror all morning, and then I started helping at the grain distribution with a winnowing fan, and my vanity melted away; write a doha.
Write a doha that says serving others is like using a winnowing fan to separate the husk of ego from the grain of the soul, and a person who does it daily sees his true face in the mirror.
mirror, winnowing fan, humility
doha pls: a bell calls people to the guru but only humble people stay to serve
bell, guru, serving
The bell calls the many to the guru, yet only the humble remain to sweep the floor after.
Please write a doha that says many come when the bell rings to receive the guru's blessing, but few stay behind to clean, to carry and to serve, and those few are the ones the guru loves.
At the ashram, hundreds attended the evening bell, but the one who stayed to wash the dishes every night was the guru's favourite; write a doha.
doha pls: forget the market of bargains, serve without expecting anything, like a peacock dancing for no audience
Everyone at the market only asked what they would gain, but the old peacock-keeper there fed the hungry without a word; write a doha.
market, peacock, selfless
In the market of the world, all trade; but the servant gives like the peacock dances, for joy alone.
Can you make a doha that says the world is a market where every act has a price, but one who serves the saints and the poor does so like a peacock dancing in the rain, without thought of payment.
Let the heart bow before the saints as grass bows before the wind, and in that bowing find its strength.
doha pls: serving saints is the fastest way to find peace
serve the holy
Every Thursday my aunt cooks for the wandering holy men who stop at our village, and I've never seen anyone happier; write a doha.

Compose a doha that says that when a person gives his time, his food and his strength to serve the wandering saints with a humble heart, the Lord shows His face through them and fills the one who gives.
doha plz: in the market you pay for dew drops of kindness but real service is free
I saw a boy in the market give water to every thirsty traveller from morning dew-cool earthen cups, free of charge, with a smile; write a doha.
market, dew, free serving
In the market, everything has a price, but a drop of morning dew is free; so is the servant's love.
Write a doha saying that selfless help is like a drop of dew, silent and fresh, that asks for no price in the noisy market of the world, and the Lord drinks in the offering of those who give freely.
My neighbour gives rides to the sick on his rickshaw at night and never takes a coin; I'd like a doha about people like him.
serve the sick

Pen a doha that says the one who goes out at night to help the ill and the lonely, giving without expecting thanks, has already received the greatest reward, for he has served the Lord in His creatures.
doha pls: helping at night when no one's watching is the real seva
The unseen hand that wipes another's tear is the hand the Lord holds.
doha pls: serving saints is like sandalwood, it makes your own life fragrant
Whoever serves the saints, like sandalwood, takes on their fragrance and gives it to those near him.
sandalwood, serving saints

Write a doha saying that the one who serves the saints becomes fragrant like sandalwood, and the sweet scent of humility and kindness spreads from him to everyone he meets, even if he himself is unaware.
I spent a summer carrying water for the old sages in the hills and came back smelling, people said, of sandalwood and peace; write a doha.
My grandmother used to grind grain on the grindstone for the shrine kitchen and churn buttermilk for the poor, and nobody ever saw her sit idle; write a doha about her kind of service.

Compose a doha that says the person who works at the grindstone and the churn for the saints and the needy, without thought for rest, is the real worshipper, and the Lord is pleased by the sweat on his brow.
grindstone, churn, serving
At the grindstone and the churn, the servant's hands become the Lord's hands, grinding and churning grace.
doha pls: grinding flour on a grindstone for the poor beats any prayer chant
doha pls: fish in a stream serve the water just by being, a person should serve others by their grindstone work

I want a doha that says the humble worker at the grindstone who feeds the hungry, and the fish that live without grumbling in whatever water they are given, both teach us contentment and the honour of simply serving.
The fisherman and the miller in our village both feed hundreds, silently, one with his fish and one with the grindstone, and neither expects a thank-you; write a doha.
fish, grindstone, serving
The fish serves the stream by living its life, the grindstone serves the hungry by turning; so do humble hands.
I want a doha saying the Lord cares less for grand gifts of the rich than for the quiet help of a poor heart; a cup of water given with love outweighs riches given with pride.
small acts of seva
doha pls: tiny acts of helping count more than big donations
A cup of water given with a loving hand is worth more than a thousand gifts given with a proud one.
A child in my street shares half his lunch with a hungry boy every day, and the rich man's big donation to the festival fund pales beside it; write a doha.
diamond, shroud, serving
The diamond glitters on a rich man's hand, but a shroud given to the unclaimed dead outshines it in the Lord's eyes.
doha pls: diamonds are nothing, the real wealth is in serving the poor, even if it's just wrapping a shroud for someone with no family
The old woman who sold her last diamond to buy shrouds for the unclaimed dead of our town is the one I call a saint; write a doha about her.

Compose a doha that says the one who spends his wealth to give a shroud to the poor dead, not even asking their name, has gathered a treasure brighter than any diamond, and the Lord accepts his offering.
guru's seva
After I started helping at the guru's kitchen on weekends, my angry nature calmed down, and I want a doha for it.
doha pls: the best way to be a good person is to serve the guru
At the guru's side, the proud learn humility, and the humble find joy.
Please write a doha that says the one who offers his time and effort to the guru, desiring nothing in return, finds that the guru's grace descends on him naturally, like rain on a field long dry.
The saint asks nothing, and so serving him is the purest offering; there is no bargain, only grace.
I'd like a doha showing that a person who serves a true saint receives something that no money can buy, because the saint asks for nothing and so the server gets freedom from his own greed.
doha pls: serving a true saint changes you, no questions
serve the saint
I carried my teacher's bags for ten years across the country, and the greatest lesson I learned was that he never asked me to; write a doha.
doha idea: helping the needy is the same as serving God
I want a doha that says the poor and the helpless who come to our gate are the Lord in disguise, and the one who serves them with kindness serves the Lord, whether he knows it or not.
serving the needy
In the face of the hungry I saw the Lord; in the serving I found myself.
A homeless man came to our gate on a cold night, and my mother gave him her own blanket and tea; later she said she felt she had served God. Make a doha out of it.
The bell tolled at dawn, and the old servant of the shrine was already up, sweeping, as he has been every day for thirty years; write a doha for him.
doha pls: a bell wakes the town but the servants have already been working

Compose a doha that says that before the bell rings in the morning, the humble servant has already swept the floors and prepared the offerings, and the Lord is more pleased by this early work than by the ringing.
bell, early serving
The bell wakes the world, yet the servant awoke before it, hands already busy with love.
doha pls: real seva has no ego attached

Please write a doha that says the true servant never counts the hours he works, never boasts of what he does, and never expects to be thanked, because for him the work itself is the reward and the thanks.
My aunt has been tending the sick in our village for forty years and if you ask her about it she changes the subject; write a doha.
selfless serving
Only the one who forgets that he serves is the true servant.

Give me a doha saying that the one who spends his nights carrying the dead, starved skeleton-thin poor, under the stars, with no relative to help, is a servant whom the Lord will honour more than any scholar.
skeleton, stars, serving
Beneath the stars he carries the skeleton of one unclaimed by kin, and the Lord holds him close.
Under the stars, a stranger carried the starved skeleton of an old man whom no family claimed, to the ground, quietly; I want a doha about this person.
doha pls: carrying the dead no one claims is the highest seva, under the stars alone
rainbird, tortoise, patient serving
My uncle served in the guru's kitchen for years like a tortoise, slow but steady, and waited for blessings like a rainbird waits for rain; write a doha.
The rainbird waits for the rain; the tortoise walks slowly; the servant does both with patience.
doha pls: serve slowly and steadily like a tortoise and wait for grace like a rainbird

Please write a doha that says the servant of the guru works patiently like the tortoise and waits for grace like the rainbird waits for rain, asking for nothing else, and in time his patience is rewarded.
doha plz: seva means giving your time not just your money
Compose a doha that says anyone can give money to the poor, but the one who gives his own time, his hands and his heart to serve them is the one who has really understood what it means to give.
My boss donates a lot to charities but never shows up, while my colleague spends every Saturday at the orphanage; write a doha about the difference.
Wealth given from a distance is a gift of the purse, but time given with a smile is a gift of the soul.
give your time
When my grandmother's hands became too weak to cook, she sat and cleaned the vegetables for the community meal, saying that was her seva; write a doha.
serve as you can
Even the smallest hand can serve; the Lord counts the love, not the size.
doha pls: you don't have to be strong to serve, just sincere
I want a doha that says the old and the weak can also serve the guru and the needy, with whatever little they have, because the Lord looks at the love behind the offering and not at its size.
My uncle plays his one-string lute at the community kitchen for the hungry and picks up the fallen leaf plates; he said that was his seva, write a doha.
doha pls: a one-string lute song for the hungry and a leaf plate cleaned up is real service
He plays the one-string lute for the hungry and gathers the fallen leaf; the Lord listens to him.

Please craft a couplet that says the singer with the one-string lute who entertains the poor at the free kitchen and the one who gathers the used leaf plates are both servants, and the Lord loves them equally.
one-string lute, leaf, serving
doha pls: a needle mends rags for the poor, that's seva too

Compose a doha that says the humble tailor who mends the garments of the poor with a needle, asking for no payment, does a work as holy as any prayer, and the Lord stitches his own blessing into that act.
With a needle in his hand the servant mends what the world discards; the Lord mends him.
The tailor at the end of our street mends the torn garments of the poor for free with his needle, and he says it gives him peace; write a doha.
needle, free mending
skeleton, lock, serving
Write a doha saying that the lock on the rich man's gate keeps out the hungry, but the servant of the Lord opens his heart to a starving skeleton of a man and feeds him, and thus unlocks heaven.
The lock on the rich man's chest keeps out the poor; the servant opens his heart to the skeleton at the gate.
A starving man, who was but a skeleton, was at our gate, and we had a lock on it that night; the next morning my mother unlocked it and fed him every day thereafter; write a doha.
doha pls: lock your valuables but never lock your heart to a starving person
yogi, sandalwood, serving
I served an old yogi for a year, grinding sandalwood paste for his prayers, and he never said a word of thanks, but I felt reborn; write a doha.
The yogi's silence is more eloquent than speech, and the sandalwood paste the servant grinds is his offering.

Make me a doha that says the humble servant who grinds sandalwood for the yogi and sits near him quietly is richer than any king, since the yogi's blessing is a treasure that cannot be bought or stolen.
doha pls: grinding sandalwood for a yogi is the best seva, who needs anything else

Write a doha that says a palanquin carried by humble bearers teaches us that the servant who carries another's burden with a smile is greater than the one inside, and the Lord counts the steps as prayers.
palanquin, leaf, serving
The palanquin sways on the bearers' shoulders, and the leaf that shelters the weary; the Lord sees both.
My grandfather was a palanquin bearer for the village bride for forty years, and he used to give his leaf-wrapped meal to any stranger who passed; write a doha.
doha pls: a palanquin bearer who carries without complaining is a real servant
serve without ego
doha pls on doing seva without wanting credit
Let the left hand not know what the right hand gives; the Lord keeps the account.
I anonymously paid the school fees for three poor children, and nobody ever learned who it was, and I think that was the best I ever felt; write a doha.
I want a doha that says it is best to serve in secret, so that no one can praise you, because the servant who serves in silence is the one whom the Lord praises before all the world.
Compose a doha that says the temple does not need our wealth as much as it needs hands to sweep, to carry water and to feed the pilgrims, and the person who serves so gains more than the donor.
Within the temple walls, the broom in humble hands is holier than the wealth in proud ones.
doha pls: sweeping the temple floor is the highest worship
temple, humble work
The man who sweeps the temple steps every morning has never been inside to pray, and yet I think he is closer to the Lord than any of us; write a doha.
The grindstone turns for the hungry, the servant's hands turn with it; so the Lord's grace is ground out.
doha pls: grindstone work for the poor is the best prayer

Can you make a doha that says the one who works at the grindstone all day for the hungry, with calloused hands and a joyful heart, has earned more merit than a hundred who sit and chant without moving.
My mother wakes up before dawn to run the grindstone for the village kitchen, and I never see her tired; write a doha.
grindstone, serving
The servant is a sword sharpened by humility; he cuts the knots of ego, and heals the wounds of others.
Write a doha saying that the true servant is like a sword that has been sheathed in humility, strong enough to protect the weak, but never raised in pride, and the Lord honours such hands.
sword, humble servant
My uncle, a retired soldier with a sword in his display case, now spends his days serving at the free kitchen, and he is the humblest man I know; write a doha.
doha pls: a soldier who puts down his sword to serve the poor is a true hero
musk deer, traveler, serving

Compose a doha that says a servant who gives food and rest to the weary traveler asks nothing, like the musk deer who gives its scent freely, and the Lord rewards him with a peace no wealth can offer.
The traveler rests, the musk deer scents the air, the servant gives without a name.
doha pls: help a traveler for free like a musk deer gives scent
A traveler arrived at our village in the rain, and the old woman gave him her own bed and cooked for him, never asking his name; write a doha, with something of the musk deer's quiet fragrance in it.
The sun was merciless, and a boy stood on the bridge handing out water to the tired labourers; write a doha about him.
doha pls: a bridge and the sun, and a kid giving water, that's real seva
Pen a doha that says the one who stands under the burning sun at the bridge, giving water to those who cross, is a servant of the Lord, and every drop he gives is a prayer.
Under the scorching sun on the bridge he stands, offering a cup; the Lord blesses his thirst for giving.
bridge, sun, serving
The winnowing fan lifts the husk of pride from the servant's heart; what remains is the grain of love.
I helped the farmers with the winnowing fan every autumn as a volunteer, and I learned more humility than from any book; write a doha.
winnowing fan, humble work
doha pls: using the winnowing fan to help the poor farmers is real seva

Please compose a doha that says the person who joins the poor in their hard work, using the winnowing fan for their harvest without expecting wages, serves the Lord and clears the husk of pride from his own heart.
The cook at our free kitchen was tested by many tasks like a touchstone tests metal, and he stirred the great churn of buttermilk with a smile; write a doha.
touchstone, churn, serving

Compose a doha that says that when a person serves selflessly, it acts like a touchstone that shows the real nature of his heart, and the daily churning of effort brings forth the butter of true humility.
Service is the touchstone of the heart, and the churn turns patiently until the cream of humility rises.
doha pls: seva is the touchstone of a person's heart, not what they say
The pilgrims received a mark upon the forehead in the evening, and the servant who lit the lamps at the shrine never took his place in line; write a doha.
doha pls: the forehead mark gets all the glory but the lamp-lighter does the work
forehead mark, lamp, serving
The forehead mark brings honour to the one who wears it, and the lamp-lighter's unseen hands make it glow.
I want a doha that says it is the humble servant who keeps the lamp lit and cleans the oil, while the others receive the forehead mark and the praise, and the Lord knows which hands truly served Him.
priest, humble helper
The priest at our village had a young helper who washed the floors, fetched flowers and never asked for a blessing, and I felt he was the true holy one; write a doha.
Write a doha that says the priest receives the people's respect but the one who sweeps, cleans and serves in silence behind him earns the Lord's love, for service done in hiding is the purest.
The priest chants before the crowd, the helper sweeps behind; the Lord smiles at the sweeper.
doha pls: the helper behind the priest is closer to God
doha pls: a needle goes through fabric and leaves, never taking credit, same as a servant
Compose a doha that says the servant is like the needle which pierces and mends the torn garments of the world, then slips away unnoticed, taking no credit and leaving behind only the mended whole.
The needle goes in and out, and the garment is whole; the servant works unseen, and the world is whole.
needle, unseen serving
My mother stitched the garments of every orphan in the colony, and no one remembers who made them but she remembers each stitch; write a doha.
serve the poor
doha pls: serving the poor is serving God, simple
Where the poor are fed, the Lord feasts; where they are served, the Lord is served.
I want a doha that says every meal given to a hungry person, every blanket given to a freezing one, and every kind word given to a lonely one is a flower placed at the feet of the Lord.
The old retired teacher in our neighbourhood tutors poor children every evening for free, and I think he's closer to God than anyone; write a doha.
I'd like a doha that says the servant casts his net of kindness over all who suffer, drawing in the weary and the poor, not to keep them but to carry them across, and the Lord loves such a one.
My friend runs a small shelter and he told me he casts a wide net so no one is left in the cold; write a doha.
net, caring for all
doha pls: spread a net of care and catch all those who suffer
The servant casts a net of kindness over the sorrowing, and brings them safely to shore.
doha pls: serving the saints is like a moth attracted to light, but in the sand of the desert, selfless
The pilgrims crossed the burning sand to serve the saints at the far shrine, and like moths drawn to a glow, they never complained; write a doha.
sand, moth, pilgrim servers
Like the moth to the glow, the servant to the saint, though the sand burn his feet.

Write a doha that says the servant of the saints is like a moth drawn irresistibly to the glow of holy company, and walks the burning sand without a thought of his own comfort, finding joy in the walking.
Compose a doha that says the servant who offers jaggery and water to the weary pilgrim in the heat, standing in the shadow of a wall so as not to be noticed, is blessed beyond measure.
At the pilgrim route I saw an old woman giving jaggery and water to the tired walkers from the shadow of a wall, and refusing all thanks; write a doha.
jaggery, shadow, serving
doha pls: giving jaggery and water to tired pilgrims from the shadows is true seva
In the shadow he stands with jaggery in his hand, serving the weary; the Lord is his light.
The sandalwood gives away its fragrance to the axe that cuts it, and the servant gives himself to those who use him; both are blessed.
Give me a doha that says the true servant is like sandalwood that perfumes even the axe that cuts it, giving love to those who hurt him, and so he finds that the Lord is his companion.
sandalwood, giving fully
My friend served in a difficult care facility for the aged, and even when the old people were rude, he stayed kind like sandalwood; write a doha.
doha pls: sandalwood scents the axe, serve even those who treat you badly
scales, fair serving
The scales of the Lord weigh not the gift, but the love with which it is given.
The shopkeeper who weighs the grain on his scales gives extra to the poor each day, and says the Lord sees the weight; write a doha.
Compose a doha that says the servant does not weigh what he gives against what he receives on a set of scales, for the Lord weighs his deeds in a balance that only love can tip.
doha pls: don't measure your seva on scales, just give
